questions.text: A train travels from City A to City B at a speed of 60 km/hr and returns from City B to City A at a speed of 90 km/hr. What is the average speed of the train for the entire journey?
questions.solution: The average speed is calculated using the harmonic mean formula for two speeds over the same distance: Average Speed = 2 * (Speed1 * Speed2) / (Speed1 + Speed2). Plugging in the values: Average Speed = 2 * (60 * 90) / (60 + 90) = 2 * 5400 / 150 = 10800 / 150 = 72 km/hr.

questions.text: A car travels from city A to city B at an average speed of 60 km/h and returns at an average speed of 40 km/h. What is the average speed of the car for the entire trip?
questions.solution: To find the average speed, we can use the formula: Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time. Let's assume the distance between city A and city B is x km. The time taken to travel from A to B is x/60 hours, and the time taken to return is x/40 hours. The total time is x/60 + x/40 = (2x + 3x)/120 = 5x/120 = x/24 hours. The average speed is Total Distance / Total Time = 2x / (x/24) = 48 km/h.

questions.text: Statement: Some cats are dogs. All dogs are animals. Conclusion: I. Some animals are cats. II. No cat is an animal. (Variant 39)
questions.solution: Some cats are dogs → all dogs are animals → some cats are animals. I follows. II contradicts.

questions.text: Pointing to a lady, a man said "She is the mother of my daughter's only brother." How is the lady related to the man? (Variant 41)
questions.solution: My daughter's only brother = my son. Mother of my son = my wife

questions.text: A man walks 5 km east, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right and walks 5 km. How far is he from the starting point? (Variant 42)
questions.solution: East 5, then South 3, then West 5. Net displacement = 3 km South from start

questions.text: How many meaningful English words can be formed with letters R, O, P, T using each letter once? (Variant 43)
questions.solution: PORT and TROP (short for tropical). Also SPORT needs S. Actually PORT and TROP = 2 words

questions.text: If in a certain language, FLOWER is written as UOLVRI, how is GARDEN written? (Variant 44)
questions.solution: Each letter replaced by its reverse alphabet position: F→U, L→O, O→L, W→D, E→V, R→I. G→T, A→Z, R→I, D→W, E→V, N→M. So TZIIVM

questions.text: A is 5 years older than B. B is 3 years younger than C. A is 20. How old is C? (Variant 45)
In a class, 60% are boys and rest girls. If 40% of boys and 30% of girls passed, what percentage of students passed? (Variant 46)
questions.solution: Assume 100 students: 60 boys (40% = 24 passed), 40 girls (30% = 12 passed). Total passed = 36, so 36%

questions.text: Find the wrong term: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, 125 (Variant 47)
If A + B means A is the brother of B, A - B means A is the sister of B, A × B means A is the father of B, then P - Q + R means? (Variant 48)
questions.solution: P - Q = P is sister of Q. Q + R = Q is brother of R. So P is sister of Q who is brother of R. Thus P is sister of R

questions.text: In a row of 40 students, Ravi is 15th from the left. What is his rank from the right? (Variant 49)
questions.solution: Rank from right = (Total - Rank from left + 1) = 40 - 15 + 1 = 26th

questions.text: Find the missing term: 2, 6, 12, 20, __, 42 (Variant 50)
If CLOCK is coded as 3-12-15-3-11, how is TIME coded? (Variant 51)
questions.solution: Each letter is replaced by its alphabet position: T=20, I=9, M=13, E=5

questions.text: P is the brother of Q. R is the sister of P. S is the father of R. How is Q related to S? (Variant 52)
questions.solution: S is father of R and P, so Q is child of S. Q's gender not specified, so son or daughter

questions.text: If South-East becomes North, then East becomes what? (Variant 53)
questions.solution: Each direction rotates 135° clockwise. East → South-West

questions.text: Statement: All pens are pencils. No pencil is an eraser. Conclusion: I. No pen is an eraser. II. Some pencils are pens. (Variant 54)
questions.solution: All pens are pencils which are not erasers, so I is true. All pens are pencils implies some pencils are pens, so II is true

questions.text: How many pairs of letters are there in "MATHEMATICS" which have as many letters between them as in the alphabet? (Variant 55)
questions.solution: Pairs: M-A (skip N), T-I (skip U) - need to check. Actually M(13)-A(1)=12. Skip length analysis needed.

questions.text: A is taller than B but shorter than C. D is taller than A. Who is the shortest? (Variant 56)
questions.solution: C > A > B and D > A, so B is the shortest

questions.text: Choose the odd one: Apple, Mango, Orange, Potato (Variant 57)
questions.solution: Potato is a vegetable; others are fruits

questions.text: If the day after tomorrow is Sunday, what day was it yesterday? (Variant 59)
questions.solution: Day after tomorrow = Sunday → tomorrow = Saturday → today = Friday → yesterday = Thursday

questions.text: Find the next term: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ? (Variant 60)
questions.solution: First letter: A→B→C→D→E. Second letter: Z→Y→X→W→V. So EV
